paragraphs.paragraph: The psalm opens with David fleeing from Absalom and describing the many enemies and rebels opposing him. Many claim that David has no salvation from God and no hope.
paragraphs.title: Flight and Distress

easy.explanation: The historical setting identifies Absalom as the person from whom David fled.

answers: The many who trouble and oppose him
easy.explanation: David says, “LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many are they that rise up against me.”
easy.q: What does David describe in the opening verses?

answers: That there is no help for him in God
easy.explanation: Many say of David’s soul, “There is no help for him in God.”
easy.q: What do many people say about David?

medium.explanation: Those who trouble David are causing him distress and opposing him.
medium.q: What does the word “trouble” mean in the opening verse?

answers: From fleeing, to many enemies, to the claim that there is no help
From prayer, to sleep, to blessing
From victory, to joy, to rest
medium.explanation: David is fleeing, surrounded by opponents, and hearing that he has no help in God.
medium.q: How does the distress develop through these verses?

answers: They claim that he has no hope or help in God
medium.explanation: The people do not merely describe David’s enemies; they also deny that God will save him.
medium.q: Why do the words of the many make David’s situation worse?

answers: David is surrounded by enemies, while the question of salvation is connected with God
David is at rest, while the people are fleeing
David blesses his enemies, while they protect him
challenge.explanation: The verses set David’s distress and enemies against the claim that he has no salvation in God.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in the opening?

answers: That the distress is widespread and threatening
That David is speaking about only one person
That the enemies have already been defeated
challenge.explanation: The repeated description of many enemies and opponents emphasizes the scale of the danger.
challenge.q: What does the repeated emphasis on “many” suggest?

answers: David faces flight, enemies, and doubt directed against him
David asks for a blessing for his people
challenge.explanation: The opening focuses on David’s flight, his many enemies, and the claim that he has no help in God.
challenge.q: Which statement best describes the beginning of the psalm?

paragraphs.idea: The psalm opens with David fleeing from Absalom and describing the many enemies and rebels opposing him. Many claim that David has no salvation from God and no hope.

paragraphs.paragraph: David presents God as his shield, the giver of honor, and the one who lifts his head. He calls to God, hears an answer from the holy hill, and sleeps and awakens with confidence that the LORD sustains him.
paragraphs.title: God as Shield and Restorer of Hope

answers: As one from whom he must flee
easy.explanation: David says, “Thou, O LORD, art a shield for me.”
easy.q: How does David describe the LORD?

easy.explanation: David says, “I cried unto the LORD with my voice.”
David says, “I laid me down and slept; I awaked.”
easy.q: What does David do after lying down?

answers: God’s protection gives David honor and renewed confidence
God’s protection causes David to flee
God’s protection prevents David from praying
medium.explanation: David joins God’s protection with God being his glory and the lifter of his head.
medium.q: What is the connection between God being David’s shield and lifting his head?

answers: The place from which David hears God’s answer
medium.explanation: David says that the LORD heard him “out of his holy hill.”
medium.q: What does “his holy hill” identify in the passage?

answers: The disappearance of all his enemies
Confidence that the LORD sustains him
medium.explanation: David can rest because “the LORD sustained” him.
medium.q: What enables David to sleep and awaken?

answers: David moves from distress and hopelessness to confidence in God’s protection
David moves from victory to flight
David moves from sleep to fear
challenge.explanation: David moves from describing enemies and accusations to trusting God as his shield and support.
challenge.q: What change occurs between the opening verses and these verses?

answers: He trusts that the LORD sustains him even while he rests
challenge.explanation: His sleep and awakening are presented as results of the LORD’s sustaining care.
challenge.q: What does David’s sleep reveal about his confidence?

answers: David cries to the LORD, is heard, and then sleeps and awakens in confidence
David sleeps, flees, and then describes his enemies
David wins, blesses, and then asks for protection
challenge.explanation: The verses describe David’s prayer, God’s answer, and David’s peaceful rest.
challenge.q: Which sequence appears in these verses?

paragraphs.idea: David presents God as his shield, the giver of honor, and the one who lifts his head. He calls to God, hears an answer from the holy hill, and sleeps and awakens with confidence that the LORD sustains him.

paragraphs.paragraph: Because of God’s help, David is not afraid of the great multitude encamped around him and opposing him.
paragraphs.title: Courage Against the Multitude

easy.explanation: David says, “I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people.”
easy.q: What is David not afraid of?

easy.explanation: The people have set themselves against David “round about.”
easy.q: Where are the people in relation to David?

answers: They set themselves against David around him
easy.explanation: The people are described as opposing David from every side.
easy.q: What does the verse say about the people?

medium.explanation: David’s confidence rests on the LORD, who is his shield and sustainer.
medium.q: What is the source of David’s courage?

answers: A very large number of people
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a great multitude.
medium.q: What does “ten thousands” mean in this verse?

answers: The threat is great, but David is not afraid
The threat is small, so David flees
There is no threat, so David sleeps
medium.explanation: Although many people surround him, David declares that he will not fear.
medium.q: How are the size of the threat and David’s response contrasted?

answers: A great multitude surrounds David, but he remains unafraid
David is surrounded by friends, but he flees
The people are afraid, but David hides
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes the size of the opposing crowd and David’s courage.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in the verse?

answers: The danger comes from every side
The enemies are very far away
challenge.explanation: The phrase pictures the opposing people as surrounding David.
challenge.q: What does “round about” add to the description of the danger?

answers: It shows that trust in God produces courage before enemies
It removes the earlier description of the enemies
challenge.explanation: After presenting the LORD as his shield, David declares that he will not fear the surrounding multitude.
challenge.q: How does this verse continue the preceding idea?

paragraphs.idea: Because of God’s help, David is not afraid of the great multitude encamped around him and opposing him.

paragraphs.paragraph: David asks the LORD to arise and save him, recalling the defeat of his enemies and the breaking of the teeth of the wicked. He concludes by declaring that salvation belongs to the LORD and that His blessing is upon His people.
paragraphs.title: A Plea for Salvation and Conclusion

easy.explanation: David prays, “Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God.”
easy.q: What does David ask the LORD to do?

answers: Smitten them on the cheek bone and broken the teeth of the ungodly
easy.explanation: David recalls that the LORD smote his enemies and broke the teeth of the ungodly.
easy.q: What had the LORD done to David’s enemies?

easy.explanation: The psalm concludes, “Salvation belongeth unto the LORD.”

answers: Remembering God’s past action strengthens David’s request for salvation
Remembering the enemies causes David to give up
There is no connection between them
medium.explanation: David appeals for salvation while recalling how the LORD defeated his enemies.
medium.q: What is the connection between David’s request and his memory of defeated enemies?

answers: The wicked were defeated and deprived of their power to harm
medium.explanation: The image portrays the defeat and removal of the wicked’s power.
medium.q: What does the image of breaking the teeth of the wicked communicate?

medium.explanation: The final words say, “thy blessing is upon thy people.”
medium.q: Who receives the blessing mentioned at the end?

answers: From a personal request for salvation to a general declaration of God’s salvation and blessing for His people
From a personal blessing to flight
From describing sleep to describing enemies
challenge.explanation: David begins by asking God to save him and ends by declaring that salvation belongs to God and blessing rests on His people.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in the closing verses?

answers: Salvation depends on the size of the army
challenge.explanation: The statement “Salvation belongeth unto the LORD” identifies its true source.
challenge.q: What does the conclusion emphasize about the source of salvation?

answers: God’s deliverance of David leads to a declaration of His salvation and a request for blessing upon His people
The defeat of the enemies removes the need for blessing
The people’s blessing causes David to fear his enemies
challenge.explanation: The ending connects God’s victory over enemies with His saving power and blessing for His people.
challenge.q: How are the two parts of the conclusion connected?

paragraphs.idea: David asks the LORD to arise and save him, recalling the defeat of his enemies and the breaking of the teeth of the wicked. He concludes by declaring that salvation belongs to the LORD and that His blessing is upon His people.
